In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of choosing the spacings between the different types of road in an urban transportation network, so as to minimize construction and travel costs, given a set of origin-destination characteristics.
the optimal design of a transportation network.
the problem of determining the optimal spacings for a grid transportation network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optimal rectangular grid transportation network has the following characteristics: (a) the network is hierarchical, (b) the spacings between successive levels of the hierarchy increase with the number of levels, (c) the spacings are approximately proportional to the square root of the number of levels and (d) the ratio of the number of links at one level of the hierarchy to the number at the next higher level is approximately constant and equal to 2.0.
the optimal rectangular grid system is a hierarchy structure with the spacings between each type of road given by the formulas derived in this and in the companion paper.
the optimal network has a hierarchy structure and that the spacing between roads in each hierarchy is approximately equal to 1.5 times the spacing between roads of the next higher hierarchy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a uniformly developed area, a rectangular grid transportation system with hierarchy structure is optimal, in the sense of the hypothesis, and that the spacings between successive levels of hierarchy can be determined from the results presented here.

the optimal spacings for an urban transportation network are a function of the ratio of travel cost per unit length to construction cost per unit length, and of the ratio of the number of trips to the area of the urban area.
, if one is to choose a network for an urban area in which all roads are of the same type, then one should choose a rectangular grid network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the problem of designing a rectangular grid transportation system, the choice of the hierarchy structure is more important than the choice of the spacings.
the optimal spacing between roads in a hierarchy is not a fixed fraction of the spacing in a higher hierarchy.
the optimal grid system is a hierarchy of networks.
